clue.text: Drunkenly bed, with hesitation, someone you shouldn't?

indicators.note: something done drunkenly is done in a staggering, disordered way, so the letters lurch out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy hesitates before taking a forbidden lover to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' reads as the verb of the surface, but it is just three letters of fodder; 'someone you shouldn't' leans on that verb, finishing the thought 'bed someone you shouldn't'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit on the side is informal for an illicit lover, a person one should not be sleeping with.

clue.text: Adder that's seen after spring

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who adds up, a person who sums
second meaning: the season following spring

explanation.surface: A snake that comes out once spring has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adder' looks like the snake, but it is someone who adds numbers, one who 'sums'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sums figures is jokingly a summer, and the warm season follows spring in the calendar.

clue.text: Rickety old car hit entrance to college, leaving youngster in cast

indicators.note: a rickety thing is shaky and falling apart, so the words that follow are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is where it begins, its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of college

explanation.surface: A battered old car crashes into a college gate and a youngster ends up with a leg in plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests a plaster cast after the crash; it is the cast of a play or film.
explanation.definitionFit: A child actor is a young performer who appears among the cast of a production.

clue.text: In the flesh, top worn by hooligan's the wrong way round

indicators.note: the wrong way round means the whole result is read from the end back to the start
something worn by a person sits on them, so one word is put inside the other

parts.note: yob is British slang for a lout or hooligan
a lid is the top of a container

explanation.surface: A thug has put his top on back to front, seen in person.
explanation.walkthrough: Yob is British slang for a lout; the top goes in after its first letter, and only then is everything read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodily can mean in person, physically present, as in being carried bodily from the room.

clue.text: It's quite possible Olympian's put inside one day

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: put inside tells us one piece is placed within another word

parts.note: taken as written
Ares is the Greek god of war, one of the Olympian gods

explanation.surface: An athlete from the Games is fitted into the schedule on a single day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests an athlete, but it means a god of Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: I dare say is a conversational phrase meaning probably, or that something seems likely enough.

clue.text: Very much like bird with clipped wings

indicators.note: clipping both wings trims a word at each side, losing its outermost letters

parts.note: a plover is a wading bird

explanation.surface: Something that resembles a bird whose flight feathers have been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' reads as 'similar to', but here it is the verb 'enjoy', and 'very much like' is to adore.
explanation.definitionFit: To love something is to be extremely fond of it, a stronger degree of liking.

clue.text: Go east by air, excited to see Ranger Smith's adversary

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and jump about into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thrilled traveller flies east to meet their old foe Ranger Smith.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Hanna-Barbera cartoon, the picnic-basket-stealing bear of Jellystone Park is forever thwarted by park official Ranger Smith.

clue.text: Considerable work for the setter

parts.note: for and to both mark the person something is given to
the setter is the person writing the clue, who refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of a substantial piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The setter' is a crossword convention for the first person, so the setter is I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, heavy book, so a weighty written work.

clue.text: Hare without basics of diet primarily eats undergrowth

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one set of letters swallows the other
primarily points to the first letter of each of the words just before it

parts.note: first letters of these three words
to hare is to run fast, to rush
w/o is the written abbreviation for without

explanation.surface: A hare skipping the essentials of its diet mostly nibbles the undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hare' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning to dash; 'without' is not a deletion signal but its written abbreviation w/o.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushwood is a mass of small shrubs, twigs and thicket growing beneath trees.

clue.text: Architectural feature's rings captivating volunteer

indicators.note: captivating here means holding captive, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: rings are round, each shaped like the letter O
VOL is the abbreviation for volunteer

explanation.surface: A building's notable detail is its rings, which charm a volunteer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex quarter-round moulding used in classical buildings.

clue.text: Sri Lankan's last bit of investment capital withdrawn

indicators.note: something withdrawn is drawn back, so the letters are taken in the opposite direction

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of investment

explanation.surface: A man from Sri Lanka pulls out the final part of his invested money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' tempts as money in the investment picture; it is a capital city, and LIMA with T after it is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are an ethnic group of northern and eastern Sri Lanka and southern India.

clue.text: For a descendant of Jacob, could God be superior?

parts.note: the question 'could X be Y?' is posed as 'is X Y?', so the verb comes first
Ra is the Egyptian sun god
the elite are the superior, best group

explanation.surface: A theological question about whether a deity might rank above everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the question 'Is Ra elite?', a rewording of 'could God be superior?'; 'be' is absorbed into that rewording.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob was renamed Israel, and the twelve tribes of his sons form the people known as Israelites.

clue.text: Mary Berry's last roulade almost collapsed

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen into a heap, so its letters land in new places
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is dropped
the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of Berry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mary Berry's final rolled dessert nearly fell apart, a baking-show disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Berry is a famous British cookery writer and Bake Off judge, so 'Mary' seems part of her name; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Lady is the traditional Christian title for the Virgin Mary, mother of Jesus.

clue.text: See 1
They might be kept dry on the outskirts of Totnes

parts.note: sec is the French word for dry, used of wine
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of Totnes

explanation.surface: Things stored in a dry place on the edge of a Devon town.
explanation.walkthrough: Totnes is a small town in Devon, England; 'kept' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Confidential matters are things people keep, so to keep secrets is the familiar idiom.

clue.text: Expose witch infiltrating church close to nation's capital

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the earlier words go within the next one

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its last letter is taken

parts.note: last letter of nation
to expose something is to lay it open
hag is an old word for a witch

explanation.surface: Unmask a witch who has crept into a church near the seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' seems to belong with 'nation's' in the surface, but 'close to nation' only gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Danish city is the seat of Denmark's government and monarchy.

clue.text: Taken aback when guards allow tablet

indicators.note: taken aback suggests being pushed backwards, so the result is read from the end
a word that guards another surrounds it, holding it inside

parts.note: as and when both mean at the time that
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Someone is startled when security staff permit a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablet' suggests a pill; it is a slab of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stela is an upright stone slab carved with an inscription, an ancient tablet.

clue.text: Understood historian's thrown us out

indicators.note: thrown out together mean ejected, so the named letters are removed from the word
out completes thrown out, the signal that something is expelled from the word

parts.note: Tacitus was a Roman historian
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scholar of the past has expelled us.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is implied or unspoken, understood without being said aloud.

clue.text: Caught husband having affairs?

parts.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
h is the abbreviation for husband
having a meal is eating it

explanation.surface: A wife discovers her husband is involved with other women.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: a husband caught having affairs is caught out being unfaithful; 'affairs?' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating is the usual word for being unfaithful to a partner by having affairs.

clue.text: Proclaim there's more to be lost from Bitcoin and the like

indicators.note: to be lost from means these letters disappear out of the longer word

parts.note: Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, informally crypto
PTO, please turn over, is written at a page foot to say more follows

explanation.surface: Announce that further losses are coming from digital currencies.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase "there's more" stands for PTO, which is removed from CRYPTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry something is to call it out loudly, as a town crier proclaims news.

clue.text: Flu panic disrupted sporting event

indicators.note: disrupted words are thrown into disorder, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fear of an illness outbreak upsets a big match.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup final is the deciding match of a knockout competition such as the FA Cup.

clue.text: Clarify a bit of gossip urgently

indicators.note: a bit of points to a short run of letters lifted from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the run straddles the two words

explanation.surface: Someone urgently wants to set straight a rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to cleanse or make pure, and clarify likewise means to clear of impurities.

clue.text: Reportedly, I decline to provide relief for viewers

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: to decline is to drop, fall or sink

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to offer comfort to the television audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewers' suggests a TV audience; it means eyes, and 'decline' is falling, not refusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye drops are soothing liquid dripped into eyes, giving relief to those organs of sight.

clue.text: Card game's somewhat American as taught

indicators.note: somewhat means only partly, so just part of the following words is used

parts.note: the run straddles all three words

explanation.surface: A card game is rather American in the way it is taught.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game for two packs, originating in Uruguay.

clue.text: Cycling nut grabs a little bit of food

indicators.note: to grab is to take hold, so one piece is clutched inside the other
cycling moves letters round in a loop, taking some from the front to the back

parts.note: a pecan is a nut
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cyclist with a screw loose snatches a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: PECAN with its first two letters moved to the end gives CANPE, which then takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury morsel served on a cracker or bread at drinks parties.

clue.text: Oddly, sleuth's sign becomes established

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: odd letters of these words

explanation.surface: Strangely, a detective's clue becomes accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: When something such as winter or rot sets in, it starts and takes firm hold.

clue.text: Is retiring accepted for one in teaching post?

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read in the reverse direction
for means in place of, so one letter swaps in where another stood

parts.note: taken as written
tuition is teaching
A is short for accepted
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Is a person who is stepping down being taken on for a teaching job?
explanation.walkthrough: In TUITION the first I is replaced by A; 'teaching post' reads as one phrase but 'post' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a job or position of employment, as in 'situations vacant'.

clue.text: See 1
Experts run away from groups of people

indicators.note: away from means removed from the word that follows, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: races are groups of people of shared descent
r is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Specialists flee from crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is a highly skilled person, someone outstanding at a particular activity.

clue.text: Subsequently, paper probes interest rate

indicators.note: a probe goes inside something, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: AER, annual equivalent rate, is the interest rate quoted on UK savings
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Later, a newspaper investigates what banks are paying savers.
explanation.definitionFit: After used as an adverb means later, following on in time.

clue.text: Talked about time in power shower

indicators.note: talked about means as spoken, so the word is taken by its sound not spelling

parts.note: a monarch's reign is their time in power

explanation.surface: Gossip about a ruler's spell holding a powerful shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power shower' reads as one bathroom fitting; 'power' belongs to the wordplay and 'shower' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shower is a brief fall of rain, so the weather word fits directly.

clue.text: One's slow to learn about cracking fantasy novel

indicators.note: cracking a thing breaks into it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Dune is Frank Herbert's science-fiction novel
c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A slow pupil is getting round to reading a great fantasy book.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a person slow at learning, the dim pupil of old classroom stories.

clue.text: After work, a tipple to take home and drink

indicators.note: to take something is to receive it inside, so one piece goes within the other
after being worked on the letters have been reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
at home means in

explanation.surface: After the working day, someone picks up a bottle to bring home and enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After work' sounds like the time of day for a drink; here it means once the letters have been worked.
explanation.definitionFit: An appletini is a cocktail of vodka and apple liqueur or juice, a martini-style drink.
